title: Multi Agent AI and Network Knowledge Graphs for Change — Ola Mabadeje, Cisco

summary: Ola Mabadeje from Cisco's Outshift incubation group addresses production failures in network change management, a significant industry-wide problem identified through customer feedback. The proposed solution consists of three core components: a natural language interface enabling network operations teams and ITSM tools like ServiceNow to interact with the system; a multi-agent system of five specialized agents (an orchestrating assistant agent plus ReAct-based reasoning agents for impact assessment, test planning, execution, and querying); and a network knowledge graph serving as a digital twin combining graph data with testing tools such as Batfish and RouteNet. Building the knowledge graph was challenging due to diverse vendors, device types, and formats (YANG, JSON, streaming telemetry). Product requirements included multi-model flexibility, instant node access, consolidated schema, vector indexing for GraphRAG, and minimal integration burden. After evaluating Neo4j and ArangoDB, the team selected ArangoDB due to existing security use cases. Data is normalized via an ETL ingestion service into OpenConfig schema, chosen for its networking focus and strong LLM comprehension. The graph is layered so agents query only relevant layers per test type. The query agent was fine-tuned with schema information and example queries after RAG-based querying underperformed, resulting in drastic reductions in token consumption and query time. A demo showed the end-to-end workflow: a network engineer submits a ServiceNow ticket for a firewall rule change, agents synthesize the ticket, generate an impact assessment, create a test plan with expected results, pull a config file from GitHub, execute tests against a knowledge graph snapshot in the digital twin, and produce a report with pass/fail results and remediation recommendations. The agentic framework is built on open standards via a collective at agency.org supporting MCP and A2A protocols. The system is currently an MVP, with extrinsic evaluation metrics being developed to map to customer use cases.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Speaker Introduction and Outshift Background
sections.summary: Ola Mabadeje introduces himself as a product-focused professional at Cisco's Outshift incubation group, which explores emerging technologies to accelerate traditional business unit roadmaps. His background is in electrical and network engineering, with the last three years focused on AI. Outshift also works on quantum networking.

sections.title: Customer Problem and Solution Overview
sections.summary: A customer raised the problem of production failures during change management and asked if AI could help. The team identified specific workflow points where AI agents could add value. The solution comprises three buckets: a natural language interface integrated with ITSM tools like ServiceNow, a multi-agent system for impact assessment, testing, and failure reasoning, and a network knowledge graph serving as a digital twin.

sections.title: Knowledge Graph Challenges and Requirements
sections.summary: Building a representative network knowledge graph is challenging due to diverse vendors, devices, and data formats (YANG, JSON, streaming telemetry). Product requirements included multi-model flexibility, performance with instant node access, operational flexibility via a consolidated schema, vector indexing for semantic search, and minimal integration burden with multi-vendor support.

sections.title: Technology Selection and Solution Architecture
sections.summary: After evaluating Neo4j and ArangoDB, the team selected ArangoDB due to existing security recommendation use cases. The solution uses an ETL ingestion service transforming diverse data into OpenConfig schema, chosen for its networking focus and LLM-friendly documentation. The graph is layered so agents query only relevant layers for specific tests.

sections.title: Agentic Layer and Open Standards Collective
sections.summary: The agentic layer is built on open standards through a collective including Outshift, LangChain, and Galileo, with a vision of global agent interoperability without heavy integration. Components include identity, schema framework, directory, composition layers, and observation. The project supports MCP and A2A protocols, with code available on GitHub at agency.org.

sections.title: Agent Implementation and Query Agent Fine-Tuning
sections.summary: The system uses five agents: an assistant agent that orchestrates, plus ReAct-based reasoning agents. The query agent interacts directly with the knowledge graph. After RAG-based querying underperformed, the team fine-tuned this agent with schema information and example queries, achieving drastic reductions in token consumption and query return time. AQL queries previously traversed all graph layers in reasoning loops, consuming excessive tokens and time.

sections.title: End-to-End Demo: Firewall Rule Change Workflow
sections.summary: A demo shows a network engineer submitting a ServiceNow ticket for a firewall rule change to accommodate a new server. Agents synthesize the ticket, create an impact assessment attached to the ITSM ticket, generate a test plan with test cases and expected results, pull a config file via GitHub pull request, and execute tests. The execution agent takes a knowledge graph snapshot, combines it with the pulled config, and runs tests one at a time in the digital twin (knowledge graph plus tools like Batfish and RouteNet). A report is generated showing pass/fail results with remediation recommendations, attached back to the ITSM ticket.

sections.title: Evaluation Metrics and Conclusion
sections.summary: Evaluation is critical for understanding customer value. The team focuses on extrinsic rather than intrinsic metrics to map back to customer use cases. The system is currently an MVP. Two key building blocks—the knowledge graph and the open agent framework—are considered critical for building a scalable system for customers.
